Pre-exceptional basic EPS: critic raised a concrete objection: You computed FY2026 pre-exceptional EPS off a pre-exceptional operating profit of £26.21m, but management’s own guidance says FY2026 pre-exceptional operating profit will be at the top of a £37–£46m range. £26.21m looks like the FY2025 actual, not FY2026. Using the guided FY2026 basis (≈£46m), EPS would be roughly (46−13.4)×(1−35.1%)/1,590.2m×100 ≈ 1.3p, not 0.52p. The proposed figure is therefore anchored to the wrong period/basis and is too low.
Net fees: critic raised a concrete objection: You under-adjust for the stated disposals. Management said “the six countries that we disposed of made around GBP 15 million per annum in fees,” yet your entire post‑guidance tilt is only −1.13% on the £849.1m base (≈£9.6m), and that £9.6m is meant to cover both H2 weakness and disposals. If FY2025’s £972.4m includes those operations, FY2026 reported net fees should mechanically be reduced by about £15m for disposals alone (or pro‑rated to the actual disposal dates), before any H2 trend effects. As a result, £839.6m is too high by at least the shortfall versus the £15m disposal impact.

That’s a concrete mismatch to the stated FY2026 basis and period.
